narrative.overview:
A near-black working environment illuminated by purple gradients, with warm off-white text and beige reserved for human attention. The user selected visible 3D executives and task handoffs; the executive studio brief records the composition. HelloRun supplies an immersive reference, not a claim of inspected gameplay or copied assets.

The scene is a working view of persisted business state. Physical robots, terminals, receding portals and a separate owner station make collaboration spatial; readable controls and task details carry the decisions.

Task handoffs use bright raised paths, directional arrowheads, camera-facing document packets and readable sender/receiver/task cards. Every observed assignment is queued; the last route persists until replaced or cleared. The twelve-step synthetic launch meeting gives every executive sending and receiving roles, beginning with CEO to Finance budget review. A responsive participant strip and matching avatar-label highlights identify both sides and their counterparts. Visual arrival never implies business acceptance.

The reading baseline now covers both applications: 16px body/forms and a 14px compact-text floor. Agent timeline filters select either the full boardroom or a single centered avatar. Recorded decisions use independent history baselines and verified routes.
keyCharacteristics: Small warm accents, with a prominent beige attention panel.
Selectable avatars and equivalent list selection.
Handoffs explain recorded changes without executing work.

rules.name: The Authority Rule
rules.body: Warm owner accents distinguish human approval from CEO review; color never substitutes for a task status label.

dos: Do preserve the separate owner approval station and CEO review identity.
Do label synthetic previews throughout their display.
Do preserve readable task details and equivalent non-3D selection.
Do keep focus visible and stop camera follow under reduced motion.
donts: Don't restore emerald as the primary identity of these frontends.
Don't animate the initial historical snapshot as new work.
Don't treat a packet arriving as approval, execution or completion.
Don't claim screenshots prove provider readiness or live gameplay fidelity.
